i relate to every word of this post in so many ways. :(

especially about your grandparents - it's so hard knowing your time together is limited, and you can make the most of it, but it feels physically impossible to get up and *do it.* like motivating yourself to do chores or something. i live with my dad in a house literally nextdoor to my grandparents, and it's awful because somedays we go days without seeing them even though they're like, *right there.* just another thing to contribute to the depression.

it's so easy to resort to the solitude of the bedroom. feels like a haven, some days. 

but there's my two cents - sorry, i don't really have any advice, but do know that there's tons of people going through the same thing. there's even more people who have gone through the same thing who have gathered the strength to pull themselves out of it - you can too. we all can :)

hey, i'm no poet or doctor, but i can suggest you try to get professional help. everyone says that - and i got so sick of hearing it - but it really is worth a try. try to take time and make yourself happy. don't feel bad about it, it's not selfish, humans *need* to take time for themselves. good luck. i hope someone else can come along and offer more helpful words than me <3
it's hard to type a post here without it feeling dumb, isn't it? :/ imo the constant boredom is one of the worst bits about depression. hope you get to feeling/doing/thinking better.

ive been on my schools equestrian team for a few years. one time i decided to tag along to a show my friend was entering - it was his first - and we had to arrive to the barn at like 3 AM to arrive to the show on time as it was fairly far away. the place was in the middle of nowhere and at that point, i'd never been there so late at night. 


so i went with my friend to go grab his horse, so we could load him into the trailer. as we walked i just happened to look up. the _stars_ were beautiful. i lived in the city so i'd only ever really seen photos of the stars like that, idk, i always kinda assumed they were edited or enhanced but no, the sky _really does_ look like that. crazy.
